newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish minister meets party leader over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Turkish minister meets party leader over scandal.

text.p: Turkish Interior Minister Mehmet Agar began a meeting with coalition party leader Tansu Ciller on Friday amid calls for his resignation in a security scandal.
Interior ministry officials told Reuters that the pair were meeting in True Path Party (DYP) head Ciller's private residence in the outskirts of Ankara.
Agar, a close Ciller aide, is at the centre of a scandal that has unravelled since a police chief, a wanted gangster and a former beauty queen died in the same car in a traffic accident last weekend.

A government MP who runs a Kurdish tribal militia that fights separatist guerrillas in the southeast was in the car and is now seriously injured in hospital. Emergency services found pistols and silencers in the vehicle.
Turkish television had said that Agar stayed in the same hotel as the accident victims in the resort town of Kusadasi last weekend, suggesting he knew of any murky relationship between them.

A left-wing party has called for a parliamentary censure motion against Agar for failing to clear up the link between the police chief and Abdullah Catli, a mobster wanted in connection with heroin smuggling and political killings.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, an Islamist in coalition with Ciller, has yet to make a public statement on the scandal.
